result.note: Cabinet-approved energy scheme with clear outlay, ministry, duration, blending obligation and pricing, plus the predecessor SATAT scheme.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about GOBARdhan, the national compressed biogas scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2026:
items: It runs from 2026-27 to 2035-36 under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
It fixes an administered compressed biogas price of INR 2,110 per million BTUs for at least ten years.
It aims to raise domestic compressed biogas output roughly threefold over the coming decade.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The scheme aims to raise domestic output nearly tenfold, not threefold, over the decade. Its INR 237 billion outlay rests on offtake certainty, with a fixed price and a notified blending obligation guaranteeing producers a buyer.
questions.source: It also fixes an administered CBG price of INR 2,110 per million British thermal units (BTUs) for at least ten years.

questions.prompt: Which scheme, launched in 2018, targeted 5,000 compressed biogas plants producing 15 million tonnes a year by 2023-24?
questions.explain: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) was the largest earlier compressed biogas programme but delivered only a fraction of its target. About 200 CBG plants operated when GOBARdhan was approved in August 2026.
questions.source: The largest, the 2018 SATAT scheme (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation), had targeted 5,000 plants producing 15 million tonnes a year by 2023-24, and delivered only a fraction of that.

questions.prompt: Under the GOBARdhan scheme approved in August 2026, City Gas Distribution companies must take a rising share of compressed biogas. Consider the following pairs of financial year and blending obligation:
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The obligation starts at 3 per cent in 2026-27, rises to 4 per cent the next year and reaches 5 per cent from 2028-29. Because compressed biogas costs more than the gas it displaces, the mandate effectively relies on continued government support to bridge the price gap.
questions.source: 3 per cent in 2026-27, 4 per cent the next year, and 5 per cent from 2028-29.
